name: Assembling the shortened name from the already-located hyphen position vs. throwing that away and re-filtering the username character-by-character
side_a: no_deduct: any construction counts for B3 — a scan loop that appends the surviving characters one at a time is just as good as substring/concatenation, as long as the characters that end up in the returned string are the right ones.
side_b: deduct: B3 credits building and returning the shortened name out of the pieces delimited by the hyphen location the method already determined. A response that discards that location and instead walks the whole username appending single characters (`result += username.charAt(i)`, `result += username.substring(i, i+1)`, `result.append(username.charAt(i))`) has not performed the required construction, so it loses B3 even when the characters it emits happen to be correct.

name: Producing the result with String operations vs. producing it with a StringBuilder accumulator
side_a: no_deduct: it does not matter what accumulator is used — a StringBuilder whose `toString()` is returned satisfies 'builds and returns the shortened String'.
side_b: deduct: B3 is about constructing and returning the shortened String with String operations; a response that accumulates into a non-String helper object and converts at the end (`new StringBuilder()` / `.append(...)` / `return result.toString();`) is not doing the String construction the item scores.
